public_rationale: The reviewed primary disclosure reports capacity growth, but it does not measure the claimed six-month deployment ratio. The searches did not establish comparable shipment, commissioning, and warehouse-inventory records for the target quarter. Later reports of installation delays would not by themselves validate this earlier industry-wide numerical claim.
limitations: Public operator disclosures use different capacity definitions.
The selected quarter is an evaluator interpretation.
Individual delayed deployments would establish neither the aggregate ratio nor widespread excess inventory.

statement.document_title: Am I Meant To Be Impressed?

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns NVIDIA data-center GPUs, rather than consumer graphics cards.
Six months per quarter's sales describes installation throughput running at approximately half shipment throughput, rather than merely a six-month delivery-to-installation delay.
Warehouse accumulation means sold GPUs awaiting deployment beyond ordinary transit and assembly inventory.
Use January–March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, as the common measurement period. Zitron did not identify a fiscal quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable shipment and commissioning data show that deploying one quarter's sold GPUs requires approximately six months at prevailing installation throughput, with corroborated accumulation of uninstalled units.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable data show installation throughput materially inconsistent with the claimed two-to-one ratio, or comprehensive inventory records contradict the claimed accumulation.
